technical_and_design_decisions: U1: Treat the NPE as a Sqoop-Teradata integration defect; root-cause it inside the Spring XD launcher and, if the bug is in Sqoop's GenericJdbcManager, wrap the job with a TeradataConnManager shim that replicates the behavior of the Hortonworks connector, avoiding a Sqoop fork.

U2: Externalize the log directory through a new configuration property (e.g. xd.log.dir) that defaults to ${xd.home}/logs, allowing it to be overridden via system property, environment variable, or xd.config.yml. Update Logback configuration to resolve the new property.

U3: Carve out a new Maven module (spring-bus/message-bus) with its own release cadence; Spring XD will pull it as a dependency. Maintain binary compatibility by keeping the existing public API and moving tests verbatim.

U4: Move the conversion service to spring-cloud-dataflow and expose a ModuleTypeConversion SPI so custom modules can register converters. Spring XD will consume the new library and provide default conversions for built-in payload types.
U5: Reuse the same spring-bus repository created for U3. Add a new spring-bus/codec module that houses codec interfaces and built-in implementations (e.g. JSON, Java serialization, Kryo).

U6: Implement SinglenodeAdmin as a thin ModuleLauncher that delegates to an in-process container instead of SSH/Container. It will reuse the existing XD Admin REST endpoints to maximize re-use of the admin UI and shell.

U7: Build a Diego-based Admin SPI implementation on top of the Receptor API (Diego's task execution endpoint). Modules will be packaged as CF Diego droplets and submitted via Receptor; the implementation will follow the existing ModuleLauncher SPI so it is plug-compatible with the singlenode impl.

U8: Scope the work as a time-boxed investigation spike. Evaluate Eureka, Consul, and Spring Cloud Services self-registration patterns. Produce a written design proposal with a recommended approach and, if time allows, a minimal POC in a sandbox project.
assumptions: The developer is already familiar with Spring XD, Sqoop internals, Maven multi-module projects, and Cloud Foundry Diego/Receptor concepts, so no ramp-up/training time is included.
A Teradata Express instance (or a JDBC-test stub) and Hortonworks Teradata connector JAR are available locally for reproducing and verifying the U1 fix.
spring-bus (U3, U5) and spring-cloud-dataflow (U4) are existing or concurrently created repositories with their own build pipelines; coordinating repo creation is excluded from this estimate.
CF Diego with the Receptor API is available in a test environment for U7; otherwise testing is limited to integration tests against a Diego in-process emulator.
The Hortonworks Teradata connector licensing permits redistribution of the minimal shim layer if required.
Standard development environment and tooling (JDK 17+, Maven 3.8+, IntelliJ, Git) are already provisioned.
No major upstream Sqoop redesign is required for U1; the fix is contained in Spring XD launcher / connection-manager selection logic.
All refactoring activities (U3, U4, U5) preserve existing public APIs to avoid breaking consumers outside Spring XD.
U8 is a research/POC spike - it does not include production hardening or full feature implementation.

activities.activity_description: Reproduce the NPE with the stock Teradata JDBC driver, trace the failure through Sqoop's JobBase / ConnManager code, and identify the missing/required connection-manager logic.

Update the Spring XD Sqoop batch job to detect Teradata JDBC URLs and use a TeradataConnManager shim, or apply the smallest code change that avoids the NPE. Include unit tests for both driver and connection-manager selection paths.

Introduce xd.log.dir configuration property, update Logback configuration files, refactor code that hardcodes ${xd.home}/logs, and add documentation. Includes verification on an RPM-style install layout.
Catalog message-bus classes, dependencies, tests, and external callers; design the new spring-bus module structure and Maven coordinates; coordinate with spring-bus maintainers on package relocation.
Relocate source/test/resources into the new spring-bus module, update package imports across Spring XD, switch XD's pom to depend on spring-bus, and fix the resulting compile errors.
Run the relocated test suite in spring-bus, re-run XD integration tests, fix regressions caused by relocation, and update CI pipelines.

Identify all type-conversion classes, integration points with the XD module loader, and extension points needed to support custom modules. Coordinate with spring-cloud-dataflow team on the new ModuleTypeConversion SPI.
Relocate conversion code to spring-cloud-dataflow, define and implement the ModuleTypeConversion SPI, and update Spring XD to consume the new module and to register its built-in converters.
Implement a sample custom module demonstrating producer/consumer of a custom domain object, exposing the new SPI so users can plug in their own converters.
Run relocated unit tests, exercise the custom-module sample end-to-end through an XD stream definition, and validate backward compatibility with existing modules.
Inventory serialization codec classes (codec interfaces, built-in implementations, configuration metadata) and assess overlap with message-bus relocation.
Create spring-bus/codec module, relocate codec code, refactor XD references, and update Maven dependencies.
Run codec unit tests in the new module and verify that streams defined in Spring XD still round-trip payloads with each supported codec.
Design the SinglenodeAdmin implementation, including in-process module launcher, container bootstrap, and how it will integrate with the existing XD Admin REST API.
Implement SinglenodeAdmin and the in-process ModuleLauncher, including module deploy/undeploy lifecycle, status tracking, and integration with the existing admin endpoints.
Write integration tests that deploy representative stream and job definitions in the single-JVM mode, validate the admin UI/shell commands, and document usage.
Study CF Diego architecture, the Receptor API, task lifecycle, and how it differs from the existing SSH-based container launcher. Document findings and design choices.
Design the DiegoModuleLauncher and DiegoAdmin implementations, including droplet preparation, task submission, log retrieval, and status mapping to the XD module model.
Implement DiegoModuleLauncher, DiegoAdmin, and supporting classes; integrate with the existing XD Admin SPI; add configuration for Diego target, org, space, and credentials.
Integration-test deploying a stream to a CF Lattice/Diego environment, verifying module lifecycle, log streaming, and failure handling.
Survey existing self-registration patterns in Spring Cloud Services and related projects, evaluate feasibility for s-c-s modules, document trade-offs, and propose a recommended approach.
Build a minimal proof-of-concept where a sample s-c-s module registers with a service registry (Eureka/Consul) and is discovered and orchestrated by an XD runtime on CF.
Update parent POMs, dependency management, and CI pipelines to reflect the new spring-bus and spring-cloud-dataflow dependencies and the relocated modules.
Run a full Spring XD build with the relocated modules, execute smoke tests for streams/jobs, and verify admin/UI behavior across singlenode and Diego modes.
Update reference docs, release notes, and migration notes covering the new logging configuration, module moves, and the two new Admin SPI implementations.
